The present study was performed to investigate if tenocyte response to IL-1 β stimulation can be regulated by cellular tension. Tenocytes isolated from rabbit Achilles tendons were seeded onto one of the following substrates: glass or PDMS-made micropillar substrate (3 μm diameter, 6 μm spacing in a hexagonal lattice with a pillar height of 2, 4 or 8 μm). Substrate stiffness was the highest in glass and the lowest in 8 μm-height micropillars. Following a 24-h incubation, IL-1β was administrated at 0 pM (control), 1 pM, 10 pM or 100 pM. IL-1β culture was performed for 3 days. Cell shapes and mRNA expression of matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP-1) in each condition was assessed. It was demonstrated that cell shape was remarkably influenced by both substrate stiffness and the concentration of IL-1 β. Cell area was significantly decreased with lowering substrate stiffness and increasing IL-1β concentration. The expression of MMP-1 mRNA was also influenced by both the substrate stiffness and ILl β concentration. These findings suggest that cellular tension, which is thought to reflect the substrate stiffness, is a key mechanical factor in the regulation of tenocyte functions, in particular their responses to inflammatory stimulation.

articleTitle: Calibration process for the Young's modulus of a mechanically trapped microbead measured by atomic force microscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: This paper reports the measurement of the mechanical property of a trapped microbead using atomic force microscopy (AFM). The influence of the AFM sample immobilization method, which is called mechanical trapping method, is calibrated according to simulation software and force analysis. The calibration accuracy is verified using some PDMS beads.

articleTitle: Real Time, Flexible RF Sputtered ZnO Nano-film CO2 Sensor for Capnographic Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this research we aim to develop a real time, flexible, nano-film CO2sensor that can be fixed inside a mask for the purpose of capnography. Capnography is monitoring of the concentration or partial pressure of carbon dioxide in the respiratory gases. Its main development has been as a monitoring tool for use during anesthesia, intensive care, pulmonary perfusion, alveolar ventilation, respiratory patterns. The shape of curve is affected by some forms of lung diseases; in general, there are obstructive conditions such as bronchitis, emphysema and asthma in which the mixing of gases within the lung is affected. Currently, capnography is done using a capnography that utilizes a set of infrared trans mitter and receiver attached to a mask, which is a bit bulky setup. But in case of our sensor, we deposit interdigitated Au/Ti electrodes on a free standing nanosheet that acts as our substrate, then further depositing ZnO sensing layer on top of interdigitated part of electrodes. Measurements can be carried out by measuring the resistance between two terminals of electrodes. Due to adsorption of CO2on the sensing layer, the resistance between the electrodes will be changes resulting in a graph, which will show the curve in proportion to conc. of the CO2in air. This sensor is only 10mm X 10mm in area and few hundred nanometers thick, resulting in a sensor of almost negligible volume and weight that can be easily attached inside a mask. Sensor has a very simple fabrication and multiple pieces can be bulk fabricated at the same time under same conditions, making it very cheap and fit for commercial use. This sensor can also detect presence of few more harmful gases and vapors like acetone, ethanol and methane. So, further we have plans to make is more selective towards CO2by coating it with partially permeable membrane or by addition of some impurity.

articleTitle: Study of a dura mater model using fiber materials
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: In this study, we focused on fabricating dura mater model for brain surgeries training, especially for a transnasal pituitary surgery. In this paper, a dura mater model was developed by combining an elastic material and a fiber material to mimic actual dura mater. The fabricated dura mater model was compared with porcine dura mater and evaluated. The dura mater model can be used to improve surgical skills for suturing dura mater by installing into a surgical simulator.

articleTitle: Wide-range load sensing of newborn's biosignals with quartz crystal resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science (MHS)
abstract: We present a device for non-invasive detection of newborn's multi-biosignals. It is difficult to detect newborn's biosignals such as weight, heart rate and respiratory rate non-invasively due to the necessity of measuring various range signals. To detect these biosignals, we developed a load sensing device which has wide measurement range using quartz crystal resonator (QCR). As results, we succeeded in detecting newborn's respiration non-invasively.
